definition: Offline learning is a machine learning training approach in which a model is trained on a fixed dataset that is not updated during the learning process.
details: This dataset is collected beforehand, and the learning typically occurs in a batch mode (i.e., the model is updated using batches of data, rather than a single input-output pair at a time). Once the model is trained, it can make predictions on new, unseen data. In online learning, only the set of possible elements is known, whereas in offline learning, the learner also knows the order in which they are presented.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. Here is the short version: Offline learning is a machine learning training approach in which a model is trained on a fixed dataset that is not updated during the learning process. The part that makes it sing: This dataset is collected beforehand, and the learning typically occurs in a batch mode (i.e., the model is updated using batches of data, rather than a single input-output pair at a time). Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. And that is Offline learning — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
